title: The Kentucky Friar

scenario.title: A dialect switch on real text
scenario.body: Apps ship fun text modes (pirate talk, a Southern drawl) that run on whatever people type, and people shout. The book checks for a lower-case "ing" and always writes "'all", so COOKING stays COOKING and YOU comes out as a half-shouted Y'all. Keep every line the book's tests check, and make the shouting work.

character.name: Brother Biscuit
character.role: a friar from Kentucky who talks real slow

tagline: Type anything and Brother Biscuit says it his way: "you" turns into "y'all" and "cooking" turns into "cookin'".

brain_blurbs.book: Chops the sentence at every mark that isn't a letter.
brain_blurbs.real: Also shouts back when you shout.

rules.test_usage: Explains himself when you ask for help
rules.test_one_syllable_ing_words: "sing" stays "sing" (too short to drop the g)
rules.test_blake: Talks his way through a Blake poem, line by line
rules.test_shouted_you: Shout YOU and he shouts back Y'ALL
rules.test_shouted_ing: Shout COOKING and he shouts back COOKIN'
rules.test_one_syllable_stays: thing, king and string keep their g
rules.test_punctuation_and_spacing_kept: Commas, dashes and spaces stay just where they were
rules.test_already_fried_is_unchanged: "cookin' for y'all" is already perfect: no change

note: The book's own Dickinson test expects "you're" to come out as "y'all're". That looks like a bug, but the test pins it, so every brain here has to do the same. Tests can promise things nobody meant.
